statement: Let d0 > 0, let I be finite or countable, let ki ≥ 6 be integers with repetitions permitted, and let B, Di ∈ C1((0, ∞)) satisfy (4.3) and (4.4) with this lower distance d0. For every sector (4.1) with d ≥ d0, use these same radial data in (4.5) and let J(S) be the functional (4.10). Suppose that K ≤ 0 and λ, µ ∈ R satisfy J(S(d, α, β)) ≥ K + λA(S(d, α, β)) + µθ(S(d, α, β)), (4.14) for every d ≥ d0, |α|, |β| < π/2, and α + β > 0. Compatible tori. Let T = R2/Γ have area N, where N ≥ 1 is an integer. Suppose N distinct sites supply compatible periodic Voronoi data with lower edge distance d0 and at most 6N face–edge sectors. Their mean-zero potential (4.7) satisfies WT(h) ≥ N(6K + λ + 2πµ). (4.15) All square-torus configurations. Assume in addition d0 ≤ d∗ = 1/(2 √ π). For every integer n ≥ 2 and every configuration of n distinct points v1, . . . , vn on Tn = R2/( √ n Z2), let h be the mean-zero solution of −∆h = 2π (︄ n ∑︂ i=1 δvi − 1 )︄ . Then its puncture-first energy (1.6), with embedded and pairwise disjoint punctures, satisfies Wn(h) ≥ n(6K + λ + 2πµ). (4.16) 19 More generally, if a periodic locally integrable field E on Tn satisfies, distributionally, div E = 2π (︄ n ∑︂ i=1 δvi − 1 )︄ , curl E = 0, then E = −∇h + c for a constant c ∈ R2, and its energy with the same punctures and counterterm obeys ETn (E) = Wn(h) + n 2 |c|2 ≥ n(6K + λ + 2πµ). The energy identity remains valid after applying the same fixed orthogonal rotation to both fields.
